problem_summary.summary: Represent a square binary grid as a quadtree, using a leaf for a uniform region and four recursive children for a mixed region.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an n by n int[][] grid. Return the quadtree root; the judge supplies Node with val, isLeaf, topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft, and bottomRight fields.
constraints: n is a power of two

brute_force.explanation: For every recursive square, scan all its cells to determine whether it is uniform. Return a leaf if so; otherwise divide the square into four equal quadrants and repeat.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A region is represented by a leaf exactly when every cell has one common value. Otherwise its four quadrants partition the region without overlap, so recursively representing each quadrant represents every original cell exactly once.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2 log n) worst case: at each of O(log n) levels, scanning all square regions can inspect O(n^2) cells.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(log n) auxiliary recursion stack for power-of-two square regions, excluding the output quadtree.

optimized.explanation: Build a two-dimensional prefix-sum table once. A square's sum then reveals in constant time whether it contains only zeros, only ones, or a mixture; recurse into quadrants only for a mixed square.
optimized.correctness_idea: For a square of area A, sum 0 means all cells are zero and sum A means all are one because grid values are binary. Any other sum proves it is mixed, so splitting it into four disjoint quadrants and applying the same test constructs the required representation.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n^2) — prefix sums take O(n^2), and the quadtree has O(n^2) nodes in the most fragmented case, with O(1) work per node.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n^2) auxiliary space for prefix sums and O(log n) recursion stack, excluding the output quadtree.

steps.condition: 0 < sum < area, so the square is mixed.
steps.action: Create an internal root and split into four 2 by 2 regions.

steps.condition: Each sum is either 0 or the full area 4.
steps.action: Create leaves TL=true, TR=false, BL=true, BR=true; no further subdivision is needed.

edge_cases.handling: The root is a single leaf with the grid's common boolean value.
The one cell is uniform, so a leaf is returned without subdivision.
Each mixed region divides until uniform cells are leaves; prefix-sum queries keep each region test constant time.
